headline: High-risk default interaction: Cursor can read/write shared workspace files and run tools, while ComfyUI is offline-only but can still be fed and influenced through files and APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read workspace files, open editor buffers, and use MCP; ComfyUI exposes files and a Comfy API. That creates a plausible file-based bridge where content from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is not proven by docs, so I choose medium over low because shared files are a default surface for Cursor.
conditions: IF Cursor opens or summarizes files produced by ComfyUI
IF ComfyUI workflows or prompts are stored in shared workspace files
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic file ingestion in Cursor for shared folders
Keep ComfyUI workflow files read-only
Use explicit provenance labels in filenames
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer between generated files and Cursor

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor reads open files and workspace files and can send context to model providers and MCP servers; ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, models, and checkpoints. If sensitive assets are placed in a shared workspace, Cursor can ingest them and transmit them outward. ComfyUI is offline-only, so the leakage path is mainly through Cursor, but the shared-file exposure makes medium appropriate.
conditions: IF sensitive images, checkpoints, or embeddings are stored in a Cursor workspace
IF Cursor forwards those files or excerpts to model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep sensitive media outside Cursor workspaces
Turn off MCP servers for sensitive projects
Use a separate local-only profile for ComfyUI assets
Review which files Cursor has open before running agents
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification; ComfyUI can also operate on local files and supports multiple instances only through its own queue model. Because Cursor shares state via the local filesystem and can auto-run commands in Yolo mode, concurrent edits to the same workspace can corrupt files or git state. The overlap is dangerous by default, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or model directory
IF Cursor Yolo mode is enabled while ComfyUI jobs are active
mitigations: Use separate directories for code and media artifacts
Pause one agent before the other writes
Disable Yolo mode for shared repos
Commit or snapshot before running either agent
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can treat prior outputs as inputs, and ComfyUI produces workflows, prompts, and generated assets that Cursor may then act on. That creates a plausible cascade where unverified generated content becomes authoritative in downstream coding or automation. The docs do not prove a strict default trust chain, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Cursor uses ComfyUI-generated files as authoritative inputs
IF generated artifacts are copied into Cursor tasks without verification
mitigations: Require manual review before reuse of generated artifacts
Tag generated files as untrusted
Keep generation outputs in a quarantine folder
Use checklists for downstream actions
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is closed-source and sends data to model providers and MCP servers, while ComfyUI is open-source and fully offline by default. The main compliance issue is policy mismatch on where sensitive media or prompts may flow, not a documented residency breach. Because the pair can be used on the same data class with different retention and transmission behavior, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated media or prompts are opened in Cursor
IF organizational policy forbids third-party model-provider transmission
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor
Use ComfyUI offline for sensitive work
Disable external model providers in Cursor where possible
Document allowed data classes per tool
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls
